Spacing and craft checks.

Catch margin errors and unfinished controls before you see a mockup.

Agent tooling · jig-mockup, jig-verify, jig-review

Theme builderTheme checkerSpacing and craft checksCraft basicsMotion vocabularyMotion recipesMotion basicsComponent checklist

When agents use this

Before mockup feedback and whenever interface changes are verified or reviewed.

Skills: jig-mockup, jig-verify, jig-review.

The static command checks ledger coverage, tokens, icon substitutes and declared interaction states. Rendered spacing needs measurements and screenshot review; this guide does not claim the historical margin defect was caught automatically.

A real finding: A chip nearly touched the card edge

Before: The person found a motion-lab artifact chip about 8 px from the left edge and almost touching the bottom, while the text used about 24 px.

After / recorded fix: The recorded fix calls for one inset on all sides, a chip that hugs its word, and the icon on the title row.

Why: Compare measured insets and inspect the actual image. A source-only token check cannot see unequal rendered margins.

Source: round-5 fix list, person, 8 Nov 2026

From README.md · Craft basics the reviewer checks before the person sees anything (person, 7 Nov 2026)

Craft basics the reviewer checks before the person sees anything (person, 7 Nov 2026)

Each rule below was caught by the person in a consuming project's mock rounds, after it should have been caught by the agents. jig-mockup checks every one before a mock reaches the person, on screenshots, not from the code. When the person catches something new, it becomes a rule here (feedback becomes a check, not a one-off fix).

CheckRuleSource
GroupingSpace inside an item is clearly smaller than space between items (at most half); groups have stronger headers and a section gap.Gestalt law of proximity; common list patterns (VS Code, Linear, GitHub)
Alignment and insetsEverything inside a container keeps one inset; controls centre on the text line; sizes on a 4 px grid from tokens.Material Design and Atlassian spacing systems
IconsOne icon set, one size and stroke per context; never text characters as icons.Common design system practice (Fluent, Carbon, Material)
Controls belong to their hostAttached controls are borderless in the host's header, shown on hover or selection; no pasted-on boxes.Figma, Miro, VS Code row actions
Every overlay can be leftEvery menu, dialog and palette closes with Escape and a click outside, and says so where it is not obvious.WAI-ARIA Authoring Practices (dialog, menu)
Identity of special actorsAnything the person talks to or that acts on their behalf (an assistant, a coordinator) is named and visually distinct everywhere it appears; test with text hidden.Familiar assistant patterns (VS Code Chat, Slack apps)
Same type, same lookEvery instance of a type carries its signature (for example every session shows its provider mark) at every zoom where it is visible.Consistency heuristic (Nielsen, heuristic 4)
Predictable placementA control for the same job sits in the same place with the same icon everywhere (every panel collapses from the same corner, every node menu at the header end), and is visible without hunting; the person should know where to look before they look.Nielsen heuristic 4, consistency and standards; Jakob's law (people expect your app to work like the others they use)
Text never sizes the shapeDistinctive shapes (diamonds, bubbles, tabs) are fixed-size badges on a normal card; text clamps to a set number of lines at a fixed width and opens in full elsewhere.Person, from Mermaid flowcharts whose diamonds grow with every word; text inside a diamond uses about half its area
Stable chromeHeaders, tab bars and frames keep one layout and height across zoom levels and states; only content changes. A reflowing header reads as a glitch.Consistency heuristic (Nielsen 4); the person, 7 Nov 2026
Scannable listsRows have a visual anchor (a leading icon column), weight contrast between name and detail, and grouping (time, project); identical rows of equal weight read as bland and slow to scan.Activity feeds (GitHub, Linear); the person, 7 Nov 2026
Styled scrollbarsScrollbars are thin, use theme tokens, have an invisible track and strengthen on hover; never the platform default thick grey bar.VS Code and macOS overlay scrollbars; the person, 7 Nov 2026
No redundancyA row does not repeat what its context already says (parent name, a glyph that duplicates its chip, placeholders such as "—" for missing data).Nielsen heuristic 8, aesthetic and minimalist design
Labels say what they doSettings and toggles use plain words with a one-line description; no internal jargon ("Motion: drift").Nielsen heuristic 2, match with the real world
Motion on every changeEligible changes explain themselves with motion instead of narrating labels; record frequency-gate rejections and reduced-motion stillness explicitly (Motion basics below).Change blindness research; Heer and Robertson 2007; person, 8 Nov 2026, two budgets and frequency gate
Depth without shadowsChrome, panels and content sit on distinct tonal layers; the active tab matches the surface it opens; one row of chrome where one will do.Material Design dark theme elevation; Chrome and VS Code tabs
No accidental plain textInterface information uses designed components; plain text only for reading content.Person's rule; see the component checklist
Visible on its groundCompare rendered ink with its actual ground using the shared visibility probe: flag empty text/marks and low contrast (4.5:1 ordinary text, 3:1 large text and graphics). Also compare the contact sheet against the reference: geometry does not prove craft. Logos are checked as a local quality rule, although WCAG exempts logotypes.Person, 8 Nov 2026; thresholds informed by WCAG 1.4.3 and 1.4.11; pixel results are probes, not WCAG conformance
